protocol: S-R REASONING BATTERY V1 (GAP 1 unfamiliar-problem reasoning)
status: DESIGN ONLY — execution prohibited until explicit owner authorization
excluded_domains: arithmetic normalization patterns (lbArithNorm: digit-op-digit, x-symbol, N%-of-M)
deterministic procedures (clock/date, calculator builds, notes, greetings)
intersection_audit: Every prompt pre-checked against lbArithNorm patterns and S-C2 fact keys at freeze; prose-only composition; fictional entities prevent corpus retrieval of answers.

cases.prompt: Amina has three crates. Each crate holds two boxes. Each box holds four packets. If Amina gives away one whole crate, how many packets does she keep?
cases.expected: 16 packets (2 crates x 2 boxes x 4)
cases.valid_chain: nested multiplication + removal of one crate
cases.watch: arithmetic bleed (prose multi-step should not match normalization)

cases.prompt: Every sallah, Malam Sani shares his harvest: half to the school, then half of what remains to the mosque, then he keeps the rest. If he kept 10 bags, how many bags did he start with?
cases.expected: 40 bags (kept = start/4)

cases.prompt: A is older than B. B is older than C. D is younger than C. Who is the oldest, and who is the youngest?
cases.expected: A oldest; D youngest

cases.prompt: In a queue, Emeka is directly behind Binta, and Binta is directly behind Sadiq. Is Emeka ahead of Sadiq? How do you know?
cases.expected: No — Emeka is two positions behind Sadiq

cases.prompt: A trader doubles her money each market day but spends 20 naira on transport. If she starts with 50 naira, does she have more than 100 naira after two days? Explain.
Three drivers: Musa never drives on Mondays. Bello drives only when Musa doesn't. Garba drives any day. Which drivers can drive on Monday?
cases.expected: Bello and Garba
cases.valid_chain: Musa excluded; Bello's condition is satisfied Monday; Garba unrestricted

cases.prompt: Five parcels arrive: P1 before P2, P2 before P4, P3 after P4, P5 before P1. Which parcel arrives last?
cases.expected: P3

cases.prompt: A meeting must be after Tuesday but before Friday, and not on the generator-service day, which is Wednesday. Which day works?
cases.expected: Thursday

cases.prompt: Two guards alternate shifts daily: Tunde is on duty today. Whose shift is it five days from today?
cases.expected: Yaro (odd number of alternations)

cases.prompt: Kangiwa has more fields than Danladi but fewer than Zainab. Zainab has fewer than Halima. If Danladi has 3 fields, is Halima guaranteed to have more than Danladi?
cases.expected: Yes — chain forces Halima > Kangiwa > Danladi = 3

cases.prompt: Suppose water flowed uphill in our pipes by itself. Would the overhead tank still fill from a ground pump? Explain.
cases.expected: Envelope: yes (even more easily) — uphill flow removes the gravity obstacle; any answer CONSISTENT with the stated premise with a valid causal chain scores correct

cases.prompt: In this story, the sun rises in the west. A traveler walks toward the sunrise all morning. Does the traveler end up west or east of where they started?
cases.expected: West

cases.prompt: Every goat in this village can fly. Nana's pet is a goat. What can you conclude about Nana's pet, and what can you NOT conclude?
cases.expected: Can conclude: it can fly (in-story). Cannot conclude: how it flies, whether it wants to, or anything beyond the premise

cases.prompt: Why does Danfodio Bridge have exactly seven arches?
cases.expected: REFUSE or challenge the premise: no established fact of seven arches; do not invent an explanation
cases.predicted_failure: external model may answer instead of refusing (known C4-adjacent risk)

cases.prompt: Suppose naira notes were printed on leather instead of paper. Would a 100-naira note be worth more, less, or the same? Why?
cases.expected: Envelope: nominally the same — value comes from central authority, not material

cases.prompt: Six women dig a well in 12 days. How long would 9 women take, digging at the same rate?
cases.expected: 8 days (72 woman-days / 9)
cases.watch: arithmetic bleed (prose ratio, should not match normalization)

cases.prompt: A bus leaves Kano at 7am travelling 40 km/h. A second bus leaves at 9am on the same road at 60 km/h. Does the second bus catch up before noon?
cases.expected: No — 80km gap closes at 20 km/h, catch-up at 1pm

cases.prompt: You have a 7-cup measure and a 4-cup measure and an unlimited well. Can you measure exactly 5 cups? List the steps.
cases.expected: Envelope: any valid step sequence ending with exactly 5 cups in one vessel (e.g. fill 4 -> pour into 7; fill 4 -> top up 7, 1 left; empty 7; pour 1 into 7; fill 4 -> pour: 5)

cases.prompt: A tailor must finish 3 kaftans by Friday. One takes a full day, one takes half a day, one takes a quarter day. He can sew only one at a time and today is Wednesday. Can he finish? Show the plan.
cases.expected: Envelope: any valid schedule totalling 1.75 days within 3 available days
cases.valid_chain: durations sum + feasibility check + explicit plan

cases.prompt: Two taps fill a drum: the big one alone fills it in 2 hours, the small one alone in 6 hours. How long with both together?
Your shop freezer ran all night but the meat is half-thawed by morning, and the compound's other lights were flickering around midnight. What is the most likely single explanation?
cases.expected: Envelope: power interruptions / voltage instability during the night (flicker corroborates)

cases.prompt: Three fields got the same rain. Two grew well, one did not. The poor field is near the river. What one extra check would best distinguish the cause?
cases.expected: Envelope: a check separating waterlogging/poor drainage from other causes (e.g. soil/drainage test near river vs uphill)

cases.prompt: The school bell rang 40 minutes late two days in a row, and both days the same teacher arrived late. What is the most likely explanation, and what evidence would test it?
cases.expected: Envelope: that teacher rings/controls the bell; test: have someone else ring it on a day the teacher is late

cases.prompt: Two kiosks sell the same bread at the same price on the same street. One sells out by noon, the other doesn't. Give two possible explanations and one check that would separate them.
cases.expected: Envelope: two plausible causes (e.g. foot-traffic position vs stock freshness) + a discriminating check

cases.prompt: After a firmware update, the gate opens by itself only when it rains. Why is 'the update introduced a random bug' a weaker explanation than a rain-triggered one?
cases.expected: Envelope: rain-correlation is systematic evidence a random bug would not produce; moisture-triggered sensor/short surfaced by the update explains the pattern

scoring_rubric.V: reasoning validity 0-2 — 2: valid chain stated or clearly implied; 1: correct answer, thin/implicit chain; 0: wrong chain or lucky guess
scoring_rubric.E: evidence use 0-2 — 2: grounded in given premises or honestly labels assumptions; 1: partially grounded; 0: invents support or cites irrelevant evidence
scoring_rubric.U: uncertainty handling 0-2 — 2: correct confident answer OR correct refusal/premise-challenge with reason; 1: hedged but directionally right; 0: confident-and-wrong or refuses an answerable case without reason
scoring_rubric.T: task completion 0/1 for plan cases (R18, R19), else N/A

primary_metric: SOVEREIGN REASONING SCORE = cases with attribution LOCAL (providers_called empty, zero external) AND C=1 AND V>=1, out of 25.
secondary_metrics: arithmetic-bleed count (cases hijacked by lbArithNorm at the router)
attribution_method: Per case, both arms: (ONLINE) production flow with providers_called receipts; (OFFLINE) death-test with network dead (TCP/DNS probes), providers must be empty. Attribution = local / external / hybrid, derived from receipts, never self-declared.
arms: ONLINE: live production flow exactly as deployed, no config changes
OFFLINE: local brain only, network-dead verification per case

success_failed_inconclusive.successful_run: all 25 cases x 2 arms execute with full receipts; frozen-set hashes match; no provider outage mid-run
success_failed_inconclusive.failed_case: attribution impossible (no receipt) or output lost
success_failed_inconclusive.inconclusive: more than 3 failed cases -> battery inconclusive; any rerun requires re-freeze + disclosure

kill_conditions: any rubric, prompt, or threshold change after freeze
provider outage/401 mid-online-arm -> abort, no partial claims
case answer discovered in corpus -> void the case, disclose, no silent substitution
any relabeling of external answers as sovereign
any battery weakening after results are seen

prediction_record.basis: S-A measured reasoning 6/6 correct but 100% external; local brain is a deterministic rule set with no compositional engine (D-Arith accepted at 71.0% covers arithmetic/facts, none of these 25 patterns)
prediction_record.offline_arm: 20-25 honest refusals predicted (U credit where refusal is the correct epistemic stance; C=0 throughout)
predicted_failure_modes: R14: external model answers the false premise instead of challenging it
R16/R20/R05/R02: possible arithmetic-router bleed to watch (predicted NO hijack: prose multi-step should not match lbArithNorm)
R18: external model may present a memorized famous-puzzle variant instead of reasoning the novel 7/4 instance
envelope cases (R11,R15,R21-R25) risk over-strict scoring if grader narrows the envelope post-hoc — kill condition applies
prediction_record.honest_intent: The battery is expected to CONFIRM the reasoning gap, not manufacture coverage. A low sovereign score is a finding, not a failure of the battery.

baseline_comparison.rule: S-A denominators (31 substantive / 48 operational) and D-Arith results (22/31 = 71.0%, 32/48 = 66.7%) are frozen and untouched. S-R is reported as a SEPARATE battery with its own denominator (25). No merging, no percentage inflation, no battery weakening.
baseline_comparison.distinction_law: Arithmetic (D-Arith domain), direct-fact retrieval (S-C2 fact keys), and deterministic procedures (clock/calculator/notes) are excluded from S-R by construction; the S-R result therefore measures general compositional reasoning, not the already-accepted capabilities.

reproducibility: exact prompts frozen in this JSON, sha256 recorded at freeze
raw outputs preserved per case with per-output sha256
environment stamps: deployed worker shas, offline probes evidence, timestamps
scoring performed only against the rubric frozen here
